newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton market closed for local holiday.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton market closed for local holiday.

text.p: The Bombay cotton market was lcoased on Tuesday for a local holiday. Trading resumes on Wednesday.
On Monday cotton prices rose despite slow mill buying on increased exporter demand.
Export enquiries focussed on medium and long staple cotton.

In spot, Bengal-deshi rose 5.0 rupees to 915/960 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Punjab saw-ginned by 10 rupees to 1,575/1,670 rupees per maund. F-414 gained 5.0 rupees to 1,910/1,940 rupees per maund. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose 200 rupees to 13,700/14,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Long-staple Gujarat Sankar-4 (superior variety) climbed up from 18,500/19,700 rupees to 18,700/19,800 rupees per candy.
Arrivals remained low on account of ongoing nationwide strike by transport operators.
Indian transporters have been on a strike since April 1 to protest against a service tax and a rise in insurance premiums.
